## Working session summary

Done. PR **https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2155** is out of draft, mergeable, and every non-skipped check is green (including `Check for Changesets`, which was the sole failure on the previous head).

**Final state of the branch** — 5 commits on top of `origin/main` (which is fully merged; branch is 0 behind):

| Commit | Fixes |
|---|---|
| `33137125` | RC-C — resolve the sidecar image before `docker run` instead of dumping raw argv |
| `4496aa27` | RC-D/E/F/H — silent launch failures now logged; UUID kept in the Telegram failure reply; refused sessions untracked; `/queue` reports them as failed, not `Finished: … (started)` |
| `279f8560` | RC-G — registry refusals classified and escalated instead of the same warning 151× over 12.5 h |
| `7a46a3ae` | RC-I — `session_untracked` records why |
| `97b034f9` | RC-J — start-command's execution UUID surfaced end to end |

**RC-J, the answer to "no way to see UUIDs" and "these tasks are not in list":** every isolated task has two UUIDs. Hive Mind mints the session UUID (`--session`, container name) and reported only that; start-command mints an execution UUID that appears in its launch banner, in `$ --status` as `uuid`, and is *the only identifier `$ --list` prints*. The two views could never be joined — the tasks were in the list, just unrecognisable. Now the execution UUID is parsed from the banner (or a JSON launch record), returned by `executeWithIsolation()`, stored/persisted/logged on the session, shown next to the session UUID in both the executing and completion replies, and backfilled from `$ --status` for sessions that predate the fix. Unparseable output yields `null` rather than a guess.

**Verification:** `tests/test-issue-2154-execution-uuid.mjs` (12 tests, each written to fail pre-fix first, using the verbatim banner from the incident log); full local suite `All 391 selected test file(s) passed`; lint and `format:check` clean.

**Not fixed here, because it isn't ours:** RC-A — `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai` is private (anonymous token probe: `401` for this repo, `200` for public peers). Reported with a reproducible probe, the `docker login` workaround and a concrete release-workflow fix at link-assistant/formal-ai#1001. Until that lands, the image still cannot be pulled anonymously; this PR only makes the refusal loud, attributable and correlatable rather than silent.

The case study is in `docs/case-studies/issue-2154/` (timeline, per-requirement audit including the carry-overs from #2146/#2119/#2130/#2059, RC-A…RC-J with quoted evidence and line references, and a `MANIFEST.md` whose 40 SHA-256 checksums verify).
